name: Two-Link Recursion for Learning-Space Families
statement: For $\mathcal H=\mathcal H_0\cup\{A\cup\{e\}:A\in\mathcal H_1\}$ with nonempty links on $Y$, union closure is equivalent to union closure of both links plus $\mathcal H_0\vee\mathcal H_1\subseteq\mathcal H_1$. Well-gradedness is equivalent to well-gradedness of both links plus $\mathcal H_0\cap\mathcal H_1\cap[A,B]_\square\ne\varnothing$ for every cross pair. Translating the links gives exact lower- and upper-root tests; with all coordinates active, an antipodal pair exists exactly when some $A\in\mathcal H_0$ has $Y\setminus A\in\mathcal H_1$.
proof: Within-side unions and tight paths reduce to the corresponding link. A cross union must land in the upper link. A cross geodesic changes $e$ exactly once at a shared state in the Boolean interval, and conversely such a state concatenates two tight link paths. The root clauses follow by translating and applying the rooted-union test.
